process_insights:
People ask why I use 5 gates instead of 3 or 10.

Honestly? Trial and error. Started with 8. Kept the ones that actually mattered.

The scanner isn't magic. It's just a checklist I'm too lazy to run manually.

Consistency > genius.

Someone asked why I share losses.

Because I don't trust anyone who doesn't. Show me your L's or I assume you're hiding them.

The newsletter isn't predictions. It's documentation.

Here's what the scanner found. Here's what I did. Here's how it went.

That's it.

educational:
Here's what I wish someone told me about trailing stops:

They're not about maximizing gains. They're about not giving back what you've earned.

Took me two years to really get that.

Quick breakdown for newer traders:

Why does the scanner use 5 gates instead of just picking 'good stocks'?

Because 'good' is subjective. Gates are binary. Either it passes or it doesn't.

Removes emotion. That's the whole point.

Someone asked why we wait for Friday closes instead of trading intraday.

Honest answer: I used to trade intraday. Got chopped up constantly.

Weekly timeframe = less noise, fewer decisions, better sleep.

Position sizing 101:

It's not about how much you can make. It's about how much you can lose without it affecting your next decision.

If a loss makes you emotional, you sized too big.

The 20% trailing stop isn't random.

It's wide enough to survive normal volatility. Tight enough to protect gains.

Took me a year of testing to land there.
past_mistakes:
Three years ago I would've bought this the moment I saw it moving.

Now I wait for confirmation. Boring? Yes. But my account thanks me.

Confession: I still feel FOMO when I miss a runner.

Difference now is I don't act on it. That took practice.

My most expensive lesson: position sizing.

I was 'right' on a stock that went up 50%. Still lost money because I sized up before it worked.

Being right doesn't matter if you can't hold through the dip.

I used to add to losers. 'It's on sale!'

Spent two years unlearning that. Now I only add to winners. Completely changed my results.

Real story: I once turned $5k into $12k, then back to $3k in the same month.

Know what I learned? I had no system. Just vibes and luck, then reality.
encouragement:
If you're frustrated because trading feels harder than the gurus make it look:

Good. That means you're paying attention.

It IS hard. Anyone who says otherwise is selling something.

To everyone who's paper trading right now:

That's not 'fake' trading. That's practice. Athletes practice too.

Keep going.

Bad day? Happens to everyone.

What separates long-term winners from the rest isn't avoiding bad days. It's not letting them become bad weeks.

If you're new and feeling overwhelmed:

Pick ONE thing to learn this week. Just one. Master that before moving on.

Trading rewards depth, not breadth.

Reminder: most professional traders have win rates around 50-60%.

It's not about being right. It's about making more when you're right than you lose when you're wrong.
signal_explanations:
New signal on AMPX this week. Let me explain what the scanner saw:

1. Momentum confirmed (not just one green day)
2. Volume backing the move
3. Theme strength (sector tailwind)

That's why it passed. Not magic - checklist.

Someone asked what 'cleared all 5 gates' actually means.

Simple version: 5 different tests. Each one filters out stocks that LOOK good but aren't.

Most stocks fail by gate 2. The ones that pass all 5? Those are the signals.

Why didn't XYZ make the list even though it's up 40%?

Because going up isn't enough. The GATES filter for:
- Sustainable momentum
- Volume confirmation  
- Sector strength
- Not overcrowded

XYZ failed gate 3. So we watch, not buy.
